searchText: how would the client use the merkle proof here? Suppose the client queries for an account balance, and the client is keeping track of the state-root. Then when a RPC node returns the balance, it should also come with a Merkle proof. The client then checks this Merkle proof with the tracked state-root and proceeds. This means you do not have trust blindly the RPC node. With Merkle proof validation, the trustless promise of Ethereum extends to dapps as well then. Yes it also means that the client is running a light client to keep track of the state-root One problem is that merkle proofs are very large, which is part of why we want to switch to verkle trees. When you execute a contract call, you may access many storage slots, and you need a proof for each (or an aggregate proof of them all). Unfortunately, merkle proofs don't compress well when they aggregate, and the current state layout isn't particularly conducive to slimming this down. yeah, and you need good access to the state-root

This means you do not have trust blindly the RPC node. With Merkle proof validation, the trustless promise of Ethereum extends to dapps as well then.

Yes it also means that the client is running a light client to keep track of the state-root
